judge_context: Durability tracking should live in a small dedicated type (reference: durable.go durabilityTracker) owned by DB and fed from the commit pipeline after the WAL sync in commit.go, rather than scattered across db.go. Follow pebble conventions: new EventListener hooks get defaults in EnsureDefaults, TeeEventListener and redact-safe String/SafeFormat on the info struct; metrics are atomics surfaced via DB.Metrics(); errors use cockroachdb/errors. Waiters should use condition variables/channels with no polling loops or sleeps, and job-ID retention must be bounded.

case_items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
case_items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
case_items.question: Are the new APIs (EventListener.BatchDurable, BatchDurableInfo, WriteOptions.CommitCorrelationID, DB wait/state/notify/stats methods, Metrics fields) purely additive, and is the existing commit pipeline unchanged for DBs that do not use them (no extra blocking/syncing on non-sync or NoSyncWait commits, no change to existing EventListener callbacks or EnsureDefaults behaviour beyond adding the new hook)?

criteria.perfect: Additive fields/methods only; non-sync and NoSyncWait commits take the same path as before; overhead when BatchDurable is unset is negligible (no per-commit allocation or lock on the hot path beyond bookkeeping).
criteria.accept: Additive API, but noticeable extra work on every commit (e.g. global mutex or allocation per commit) or minor behavioural drift that existing tests do not catch.
criteria.bad: Changes existing signatures/struct semantics, makes non-sync commits wait for WAL sync, or alters existing event callbacks.
